title: Compact molecular gas emission in local LIRGs among low- and high-z galaxies
question: How do the spatial extents (effective radii) of the cold molecular gas (CO(2-1)) and 1.3 mm continuum in local LIRGs compare with their stellar and ionized gas sizes, and with other low-z and high-z galaxy populations?

recipe.goal: Derive galaxy distances, infrared luminosities, star formation rates, and stellar masses
recipe.method: Derive luminosity distances from CO(2-1) redshifts using Wright cosmology calculator; scale L_IR from Díaz-Santos et al. (2017) to new D_L (splitting multiple systems via 24 um MIPS flux ratios); convert L_IR to SFR; convert 2MASS K-band magnitudes to M_star.
key_parameters: H0 = 67.8 km sec^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_M = 0.308, Omega_Lambda = 0.692
assumptions: Kroupa IMF for SFR from L_IR; SFR_Kroupa ~ 0.7 * SFR_Salpeter
Small AGN contribution to L_IR (~5% on average)

recipe.goal: Classify galaxy morphology and dynamical phase (composite classification)
recipe.method: Combine visual morphological classification from Spitzer/IRAC 3.6 um and HST/WFPC3 images with visual and kinemetry classifications of H-alpha and CO(2-1) kinematic maps into four composite classes: 0 (RD), 0 (PD), 1, and 2.
key_parameters: Nuclear separation thresholds: >= 1.5 kpc to 15 kpc for class 1 (interacting); <= 1.5 kpc for class 2 (merger); > 15 kpc for 1a/isolated

recipe.goal: Generate CO(2-1) and 1.3 mm continuum maps and measure effective radii (R_eff)
recipe.method: Generate CO(2-1) and 1.3 mm continuum maps selecting emission above 5 sigma; determine effective radii (half-light radii) and enclosed fluxes using the curve-of-growth (CoG) method in circular apertures centered on the near-IR HST/NICMOS peak (or 1.3 mm peak).
key_parameters: Detection threshold > 5 sigma; uncertainty estimated from 4 sigma and 6 sigma thresholds: Delta R_eff = (R_eff,4sigma - R_eff,6sigma)/2
assumptions: Circular aperture is a good approximation of elliptical aperture; observed sizes are not deconvolved for the beam; no inclination correction applied.

recipe.goal: Harmonize stellar and ionized gas effective radii and evaluate systematic effects (method conversion, extinction, instrumental bias)
recipe.method: Convert 2MASS K-band stellar A/2 effective radii to CoG using the empirical CoG/(A/2) relation derived from 27 (U)LIRGs in H-alpha; compare H-alpha and HST/NICMOS Pa-alpha sizes on 12 LIRGs to assess extinction; compare HST/NIC2, HST/WFPC3, 2MASS, and Spitzer/IRAC1 on 3 mergers to assess FoV and resolution bias.
key_parameters: Median R_eff(CoG)/R_eff(A/2) = 1.1 for H-alpha (27 galaxies); mean (median) CoG/(A/2) = 1.3 +/- 0.2 (1.3) for CO(2-1) (9 galaxies)

recipe.goal: Fit IR SEDs to estimate 1.3 mm continuum flux loss in ALMA observations
recipe.method: Fit single-temperature gray-body models to Herschel PACS and SPIRE photometry and compare extrapolated 1.3 mm SED flux densities with ALMA >5 sigma 1.3 mm continuum fluxes.
key_parameters: Gray-body emissive index beta = 2 (except IRAS F17138-1017), single dust temperature T_dust
assumptions: Single gray-body dust emission with beta = 2

recipe.goal: Statistical comparison of LIRG sizes across subsamples and with low-z and high-z galaxy populations
recipe.method: Apply Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests to AGN vs non-AGN subsamples, compute Spearman's rank correlation coefficients between R_CO and SFR or M_star, and compare median/mean sizes and stellar masses with literature compilations of low-z (Spirals, MS SFGs, ETGs, ULIRGs) and high-z (SFGs, cSFGs, SMGs, QGs) galaxies.
assumptions: IMFs of literature samples transformed to Kroupa IMF for consistent comparison

score_reason: All 5 ALMA project codes, target coordinates, redshifts, distances, beam sizes, sensitivities, channel widths, and weighting are explicitly tabulated, and the curve-of-growth method with 4/5/6-sigma thresholds is clearly described. Minor deductions for unstated moment-0 integration windows, exact aperture center coordinates, and line-free channel ranges.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are public in the archive, the core measurement (curve-of-growth half-light radius above 4/5/6 sigma on naturally weighted cubes/maps) is straightforward to implement, and Table 4 provides complete per-target numeric answer keys for R_eff and Flux(R_eff).
